recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-16971; future Common Languages additions or spelling corrections should remain separate terminology-maintenance trackers.
issue_request: FHIR-16971 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 and asked to resolve Attachment.language's broken "Common Languages (Extensible but limited to ??)" wording. The accepted resolution was to fix the broken link while keeping Common Languages as a useful enumerable construct.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn 14306, which maps to git commit bfae89f160d2798001c532d9b7287299aa6ea82b. That commit updated datatype/link generation and TerminologyNotesGenerator so a known max ValueSet rendered as a real link rather than "??".
additional_context: The language binding model later evolved from extensible Common Languages plus max All Languages to a required binding to All Languages with an additional starter binding to Common Languages. Applied decisions including FHIR-46074 and FHIR-46350 support that current model.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Attachment.language uses the shared Language binding, the current Language binding row is required to valueset-all-languages with starter=valueset-languages, and no current Attachment.language source contains the broken "limited to ??" text.

related_jiras.note: TerminologyCapabilities adopted the same required All Languages binding plus Common Languages starter set pattern.
Later FHIR-I guidance confirmed that required/maximal bindings should be primary and narrower common/preferred lists should be additional bindings.
Later Resource.language reconciliation aligned narrative wording to the same all-languages plus common-languages starter model.
